question: Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem at work.
answer: I was a receptionist at a dental practice and patients kept arriving for appointments that were not in the diary. I went back through two weeks of bookings and asked each of those patients how they had booked. All of them had booked online on a Sunday, and I found the online diary was closed on Sundays, so those bookings were being accepted on screen but never saved. As that was the cause, I asked the practice manager to have Sunday booking switched on, and in the meantime I added a line to the reminder text saying to book on weekdays. After that we had no more patients turning up without an appointment.
reason: Clean base answer: gathers information, states the cause, links the action to it and states the result; level 3 Problem Solving evidence.

question: Describe a time you worked with others to reach a shared goal.
answer: Four of us on a village football club committee had to raise the money for a new set of goals before the season started. I was the treasurer, so I kept the running total and sent it round to the others every Sunday night so we all knew how far off we were. When the sponsored walk was rained off and we were still short, I asked the two coaches if they would help me run a cake stall at the next three home games, and they did. We reached the total with a week to spare and the goals were up for the first match.
